# Harbormaster: a guide for LLM agents

This is a single-page reference for an agent that sets up a Harbormaster deployment, or
converts a Docker Compose app to run under Harbormaster. It is complete enough to work
from on its own. Full documentation: https://harbormaster.readthedocs.io/


## What Harbormaster is

Harbormaster runs several Docker Compose apps on one host. You give it a YAML file that
lists git repositories, each containing a Compose app. It clones them, runs `docker
compose up` on each one, and restarts an app when its repository or its configuration
changes.

It is not a daemon. The operator runs `harbormaster run` on a timer (cron, a systemd
timer, or the bundled container). Each run brings every app to its desired state and
exits.

Harbormaster does not provide ingress, a reverse proxy, TLS, or DNS. If the app needs to
be reachable from outside, that is the operator's job. It also does not schedule across
hosts; everything runs on the machine where it is invoked.


## The working directory

Harbormaster keeps everything under one directory, so that the whole deployment can be
backed up and restored as a unit:

- `harbormaster.yml` - the configuration file. It may live elsewhere, see `-c`.
- `repos/<app_id>/` - the app's git checkout. Harbormaster owns this; do not edit files
  here, they are overwritten on the next pull.
- `data/<app_id>/` - data to keep. Never deleted. When an app is removed from the
  config, this is moved to `archives/<app_id>-<timestamp>`.
- `caches/<app_id>/` - data that can be thrown away. Deleted when the app is removed
  from the config. Note the directory is `caches`, plural.
- `archives/` - the data directories of removed apps.
- `.harbormaster.cache` - internal state, used to notice configuration changes.

`<app_id>` is the key you give the app in the config file.


## The configuration file

```yaml
config:
  prune: false
apps:
  myapp:
    url: https://github.com/someuser/myapp.git
    branch: main
    manage_volumes: true
    environment:
      TZ: Europe/Athens
    environment_file: secrets/myapp.txt
  otherapp:
    url: https://github.com/someuser/otherapp.git
    manage_volumes: true
    compose_config:
      - docker-compose.yml
      - docker-compose.harbormaster.yml
  oldapp:
    enabled: false
    url: https://github.com/someuser/oldapp.git
```

Top level:

- `config.prune` (bool, default `false`) - run `docker system prune --all --force` after
  the run. This deletes every unused image on the host, not only Harbormaster's. Leave
  it off unless the operator asks for it.

Per app:

- `url` (string, **required**) - the git URL to clone.
- `branch` (string, default `master`) - the branch to deploy. The default is `master`,
  not `main`, so set this explicitly for any repository that uses `main`.
- `enabled` (bool, default `true`) - if `false`, the app is stopped and not pulled.
- `manage_volumes` (bool, default `false`) - let Harbormaster back the app's named
  volumes with directories in `data/` and `caches/`. **Strongly recommended: set this to
  `true`.** See "Volumes" below.
- `compose_config` (string or list of strings) - the Compose file(s) inside the
  repository, relative to its root, in the order Compose should merge them. If omitted,
  Harbormaster discovers one file, see "Finding the Compose file".
- `environment` (mapping) - environment variables for the Compose run. Values are
  converted to strings, so quote anything that YAML would read as a number, bool or
  date.
- `environment_file` (string) - a file to read more environment variables from, relative
  to the directory holding the Harbormaster config file, not the repository. A `.yml` or
  `.yaml` extension means the file is a YAML mapping of strings to strings; any other
  extension means `key=value` lines. Plain files do not support comments: a line without
  an `=` is a fatal error. Keys in `environment` win over keys in the file. Both lose to
  `HM_DATA_DIR`, `HM_CACHE_DIR` and `HM_REPO_DIR`, which Harbormaster always sets itself.
- `replacements`, `replacements_file` - legacy template variables. They still work. Do
  not use them in new configurations.

Two apps may use the same `url`, with different branches or different
`compose_config` values. The app id, not the URL, identifies an app.

An app is stopped and started again when its repository has new commits, or when
anything in its config stanza changes (including its environment). Otherwise it is left
running.


## Finding the Compose file

If `compose_config` is not set, Harbormaster looks in the repository root for
`compose.yaml`, `compose.yml`, `docker-compose.yaml`, `docker-compose.yml`, in that
order, and uses the first one it finds. Discovery resolves to exactly one file.
Harbormaster never picks up an override file such as `compose.override.yaml` by itself.

An app that needs more than one file must list every file in `compose_config`, in merge
order. The same applies to a file whose name is not in the list above.


## Volumes

Set `manage_volumes: true` and declare plain named volumes. This is the recommended way
to mount an app's data:

```yaml
services:
  main:
    image: myapp
    volumes:
      - config:/config
      - cache-transcode:/transcode

volumes:
  config:
  cache-transcode:
```

Harbormaster rewrites the volume definitions in its checkout of this file, so each
volume is backed by a directory on the host:

- `config` is backed by `data/myapp/config`.
- `cache-transcode` is backed by `caches/myapp/cache-transcode`, because the name starts
  with `cache-`. Every other name goes under `data/`.

The Compose file stays valid Compose, so a manual `docker compose logs` or `docker
compose up` works in the repository directory with no Harbormaster variables to set
first. Pass the same `-f` files that the app's `compose_config` lists, and any variables
from its `environment`, if you need the manual command to match Harbormaster's exactly.

Rules to respect when writing the Compose file:

- A managed volume's name becomes a directory name. Use plain names. A name containing
  `/` or `\`, or a name that is `.` or `..`, makes Harbormaster refuse to start the app.
- A volume that declares its own `driver`, `driver_opts`, `external` or `name` is left
  untouched. Use that to opt a single volume out.
- Do not add `container_name` to any service. Harbormaster finds an app's containers
  through Compose, and a fixed container name can stop it from restarting the app.

Turning `manage_volumes` on for an app that is **already running** with plain named
volumes does not migrate the old data. Docker keeps that data under its own name,
`<project>_<volume>`, while Harbormaster creates and mounts fresh directories, so the
app normally comes up empty and unwarned. Moving the data is a manual job. Harbormaster
only refuses to start if a volume named exactly `hm_<app_id>_<volume>` already exists
without its own `com.harbormaster.app` label. For a new app there is nothing to migrate.

### The older approach

Before managed volumes, apps mounted Harbormaster's directories by writing its paths
into the Compose file. These variables are always set in the Compose environment:

- `${HM_DATA_DIR}` - the app's directory under `data/`.
- `${HM_CACHE_DIR}` - the app's directory under `caches/`.
- `${HM_REPO_DIR}` - the app's checkout under `repos/`.

```yaml
    volumes:
      - ${HM_DATA_DIR}/my_data:/some_data_dir
      - ${HM_CACHE_DIR}/my_cache:/some_cache_dir
```

This still works and is not going away, but do not write new apps this way. The drawback
is that any Compose command run by hand then needs those variables set. Managed volumes
exist to avoid that.

`${HM_REPO_DIR}` is the exception: managed volumes have no equivalent, so it stays the
way to mount the app's own repository into a container. It is rarely needed.


## Commands

`harbormaster run` - bring every app to its desired state, then exit.

- `-c`, `--config PATH` - the configuration file. Default `harbormaster.yml`.
- `-d`, `--working-dir PATH` - the directory holding `repos/`, `data/` and the rest.
  Default `.`.
- `-f`, `--force-restart` - restart every app, even unchanged ones.

When a run starts an app, it does `docker compose pull --ignore-buildable` and then
`docker compose up --remove-orphans --build --detach`, in the app's checkout, with `-f`
for each of the app's Compose files. An app that is running and unchanged is left alone,
so most runs issue no Compose commands for it at all.

`harbormaster test` - run the Compose app in the current directory, without a
Harbormaster config file and without committing anything. Use it to check a conversion.

- `-d`, `--working-dir PATH` - where to put the data and cache directories. Defaults to
  a fresh temporary directory.
- `-c`, `--compose-file PATH` - the Compose file to use. Repeatable. If omitted, the
  file is discovered as described above.
- `-e`, `--environment KEY=VALUE` - an environment variable. Repeatable.
- `-v`, `--environment-file PATH` - an environment file.

Test mode does not turn on managed volumes, so an app that relies on them runs with
ordinary Docker named volumes under `harbormaster test`. It checks the Compose file and
the app, not Harbormaster's volume rewriting.

`harbormaster --debug run` prints what it is doing, including the resolved Compose
files.


## Worked example

The app's repository, `docker-compose.yml`:

```yaml
services:
  main:
    image: ghcr.io/someuser/myapp:latest
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - 8080:8080
    environment:
      - APP_SECRET
    volumes:
      - config:/config
      - cache-thumbnails:/thumbnails

volumes:
  config:
  cache-thumbnails:
```

The deployment repository, `harbormaster.yml`:

```yaml
apps:
  myapp:
    url: https://github.com/someuser/myapp.git
    branch: main
    manage_volumes: true
    environment_file: secrets/myapp.txt
```

`secrets/myapp.txt`, next to `harbormaster.yml`:

```
APP_SECRET=replace-me
```

Result: the app is checked out to `repos/myapp/`, its config lives in `data/myapp/config`
and its thumbnails in `caches/myapp/cache-thumbnails`. Both are plain host directories.


## Checklist before you finish

- `manage_volumes: true` is set, and the Compose file uses plain named volumes.
- `branch` is set if the repository does not use `master`.
- No service declares `container_name`.
- Every Compose file is listed in `compose_config` if there is more than one.
- Volume names are plain, and cache-only volumes start with `cache-`.
- `environment_file` paths are relative to the Harbormaster config file, and plain
  (non-YAML) ones contain no comment lines.
- Secrets are not written into `harbormaster.yml` if the deployment repository is shared.
- When several Compose files are merged, later files win. Where a service in a later
  file must mount somewhere else, declaring a separate volume and pointing the app's
  command at it is clearer than relying on the merge.
